subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: The Bear and Resurrection
description: A quick, practical guide to The Bear and Resurrection.

hook.text: Bears hibernate all winter and emerge in spring. Ancient people saw a creature that died and came back to life.

buildup.text: Bear cults are among the oldest in human history. Neanderthals may have arranged bear skulls ritually.

discovery.text: In Finnish myth, the bear was so sacred its name couldn't be spoken. They called it 'honey-paw' instead.

twist.text: The constellation Ursa Major—the Great Bear—is recognized across cultures. The bear lives in the sky forever.

climax.text: The bear embodies the cycle of death and return. Hibernation looked like resurrection before anyone wrote scripture.

punchline.text: Sleep all winter. Rise in spring. Repeat.

quiz.question: Why was the bear's true name avoided in Finnish mythology?
options: They feared it would summon one
The bear was too sacred to name directly
They didn't have a word for it
